dedupe_keys.name: green urban scenarios gus agent based digital twin of urban forests

description: Green Urban Scenarios (GUS) is an open source framework that builds agent-based digital twins of urban trees and forests to forecast how green infrastructure portfolios develop and what benefits they deliver under different conditions. It covers scenarios varying weather, maintenance regimes, species composition, spatial distribution and exposure to disease, representing individual trees as agents whose digital versions are built from Earth observation, street view images, field surveys and project typologies, with machine learning and statistical models calibrating biomass growth and carbon. It was developed by Bulent Ozel and co-authors and described in Arboriculture and Urban Forestry, volume 50, issue 1; the Python package pyGUS is at version 2.2.1 (March 2024). The code is available from GitHub and PyPI under the Apache 2.0 licence, free of charge. Caveats: the article presents simplified urban forest planning schemes, and calibration for a new city needs local tree data. It is useful for planning and maintaining urban tree planting as green infrastructure for heat, carbon and climate adaptation, and for digital twin prototypes; a related record is the i-Tree model suite.
